title: Diamond Trophy: Quest for the Golden Trophy
summary: Diamond Trophy is its own dedicated minigame server that recreates the Rec Room co-op dungeon crawl "Quest for the Golden Trophy" almost 1:1. A party of 1 to 20 players gears up in an armory and fights through 9 linear acts of a goblin army's waves before facing the Goblin King. Runs are scored on gold and given a letter rating (S/A/B/C), which pays out currency and XP; a social dorm area between runs has a training dummy and a bouncing basketball toy.
how_it_works:
Getting a group together: every player has a private dorm room (up to 4 people) reached with /dormroom, where you can invite friends, mess around with a training dummy and a bouncing basketball, and then launch a run together. You can also skip the dorm and use the FistWatch menu's room tiles to join a public matchmaking room (grouped up with strangers) or make a private one (invite-only) through the pre-game lobby system - you can freely switch between waiting rooms until the run actually starts.

Room size scales with rank: a room's player limit is set by the highest-ranked member currently inside it - base (no rank) is 4, VIP raises it to 6, MVIP to 10, Elite to 15, and Champion or staff to 20. Two ranked players don't stack the bonus; only the single highest one counts. If the player propping up a big room's limit leaves, nobody already inside is removed, but the room stops admitting new players until headcount drops back under 4. If someone in your room is griefing or AFK, /votekick <player> starts a room-wide vote (cast yours with /votekick yes or /votekick no); it needs a majority with a small minimum number of votes to pass.

Gearing up: Diamond Trophy has no fixed class or loadout menu. Instead, once your room is inside the armory, you grab weapons for free from wall-mounted weapon racks - a sword, bow, crossbow or shield each. A rack only gives out one weapon until the next run restocks it. Swords can dual-wield an offhand copy for a lighter side-attack; a shield can be carried alongside any weapon; a sword and a bow can't be held at the same time, but a crossbow can be paired with a sword since it only takes one hand to fire. Bows and crossbows never run dry mid-run.

The 9 acts: opening the armory door once everyone has gathered begins Act 1, and the run moves through a fixed sequence of 9 themed rooms (The Gates, The Courtyard, The Ramp, The Bridge, The Split Path, The Library, The Maze, The Lava Room, and finally The Boss Arena) with the goblin army escalating the whole way. Some waves spawn the instant you walk into a trigger area, others spawn automatically once the previous wave is fully cleared; every act needs the whole room to gather at its exit door together before it unlocks and the next act begins.

The goblin army (7 enemy types, verified against the live mob/combat config):
- Goblin - the basic melee grunt. Deals contact damage only while standing at roughly the same height as you (stand a full block above one and it can't touch you), can't jump onto 1-block ledges, and is stunned by an arrow hit (falls over, briefly unconscious). First seen Act 1.
- Imp - a small flying-rigged enemy that never melees; it locks onto the nearest player and, after a half-second-plus telegraph, fires one slow fireball from any range. Stunned by arrows like a Goblin. First seen Act 2.
- Goblin Knight - a heavily armored halberd-wielder. Cannot be hit from the front (frontal hits just clank off - only back hits count) and cannot be stunned by arrows. Its telegraphed swing hits everyone in a 150-degree arc in front of it and knocks them down in one hit (no 2-hit buffer, unlike Goblins/Imps), then it lunges forward roughly 3 blocks and freezes in place for 2 seconds - that freeze, back exposed, is the safe window to punish it. First seen Act 4.
- Elite Goblin - like a Goblin, but immune to arrow stuns, so ranged players have to fall back on melee or kiting. First seen Act 5.
- Elite Imp - like an Imp but fires 5 fireballs in a spread instead of 1; still falls over when hit by an arrow. First seen Act 5.
- Elite Goblin Knight - the Goblin Knight's tougher sibling: instead of a single directional swing it does a four-part 360-degree spinning attack (front-right, back-right, back-left, front-left in sequence) that can catch you no matter where you're standing, then freezes for a full 3 seconds afterward - still back-only damageable, still one-hit knockdown, but never dashes (it spins in place). First seen Act 6.
- Goblin King - the Act 9 boss; see its own act entry below.

Most enemy hits only knock you down after 2 hits, but Goblin Knights, Elite Goblin Knights and the Goblin King's telegraphed attacks always knock you down in one. A downed teammate isn't gone - right-click them to revive them to full health (the community nickname for this, inherited from the Rec Room original, is the 'high five'). If every player in the room is downed at once, the message is blunt - 'All players are down! The quest has failed.' - and the run ends there. Hitting a teammate by accident deducts a 2,000-gold penalty from the team instead of dealing damage, so watch your swings in a crowd. A normal Minecraft shield still blocks incoming melee hits.

Breaking the pot furniture scattered through the acts pays a small one-off gold bonus per pot (25 for a small pot, 50 for a large one) to whoever breaks it, and killing an enemy pays gold based on its type: 450 for a Goblin, 500 for an Imp, 850 for an Elite Goblin or Elite Imp, 1,500 for a Goblin Knight, 2,000 for an Elite Goblin Knight, and 5,500 for the Goblin King himself.

Act 3's rolling boulder (a Rec Room homage) can be pushed by walking into it or launched further by punching it; it picks up speed downhill and instantly squashes any Goblin, Elite Goblin, Imp, Elite Imp, Goblin Knight or Elite Goblin Knight it rolls over fast enough, crediting the kill (and its gold) to whoever last pushed it. It never hurts players.

Act 8's lava floor has a safety net: falling in cancels the fall damage, cancels the game's usual instant-death-in-lava rule, and teleports you back to the last solid ground you stood on (knocked down, so a teammate still needs to revive you) instead of killing you outright - fall in three times in a row while already downed, though, and you're sent back to the act's start point instead.

Bigger rooms, tougher boss: the Goblin King's health rises with every player over the 4-player base, topping out at roughly three times his normal health in a full 20-player room, so a large room still has a real final fight instead of a stomp.

Scoring and payout: breaking pots and downing enemies builds your personal gold total for the run. At the end, your team's gold-per-player average is checked against thresholds for a final quest rating - S at 25,000+, A at 18,750+, B at 12,500+, and C below that - shown on the results screen alongside the team's total gold (a 20-player room is rated on the same per-player bar as a solo run, so a big room can't coast to an S on raw headcount). Clearing each act and finishing the run both pay three things at once - Diamond Trophy score coins (roughly 1 coin per 1,000 gold earned, plus a flat 5 coins per act cleared and a 25-coin bonus for clearing all 9, spendable only on Diamond Trophy weapon skins), ReimaginedCraft network coins (30 per act cleared, plus an end-of-run bonus of 160/120/80/40 for an S/A/B/C rating), and progression XP feeding both Diamond Trophy's own level track and the account-wide network level. See the currencies and levels-achievements systems for how those payouts work network-wide.

Between runs: score coins earned here can only be spent on Diamond Trophy weapon skins - cosmetic reskins of the sword, bow, crossbow and shield, sold from a physical wall of framed weapons in the armory. Right-clicking a framed skin shows its price and a buy prompt in chat; skins you own can then be equipped from the FistWatch's Bag screen. See the items file for the specific skins on sale. The dorm's basketball is purely a for-fun physics toy in the same social space - see the items file for how it works.
how_to_access: Travel to the Diamond Trophy server via the Hub's server selector or an NPC (this plugin does not handle proxy routing itself). Once there: the FistWatch item, automatically placed in the last hotbar slot, is the main menu for everything outside combat - right-click it to open. /gt or /goldentrophy covers joining, leaving, starting and following a run. /dormroom or /room returns you to your private dorm. /party invite|accept|decline|list|kick|leader (or the /invite shortcut) manage your group. /votekick <player>, then /votekick yes|no, lets a room vote out a disruptive player.

entries.name: Act 1: The Gates
entries.description: The opening act, fought just outside the armory - a pure introduction to the wave system with no enemy variety yet. Five waves in total, all of them Goblins: two are area-triggered (2, then 4 Goblins as you push forward) and the last three fire back-to-back the moment the previous one dies (4, then 3, then 4 more) in the final room, so don't wander off thinking the fight is over after the first lull. 17 Goblins in total across the act. Since Goblins only land contact damage at roughly your own height, standing on any ledge a block or more above one keeps you completely safe from it while you finish it off.
entries.how_to_get: Begins automatically once your whole room gathers at the armory door and it unlocks.
entries.how_to_use: Clear all 5 waves of Goblins, then gather at the exit door with your team to move on to Act 2.
entries.icon_hint: a pair of tall stone dungeon gates cracked open, with a small goblin silhouette peeking through

entries.name: Act 2: The Courtyard
entries.description: An open courtyard that introduces the Imp - the game's first ranged enemy, locking on and lobbing a slow fireball from any distance after a visible wind-up. Six waves mix Imps and Goblins with escalating group sizes (from a pair of Imps up to a final wave of 4 Goblins + 3 Imps), so it's the first act where you have to watch two threat types - something in melee range and something shooting from across the room - at once. An arrow hit stuns either type just as well as it does a Goblin.
entries.how_to_use: Clear all 6 waves, then gather at the exit door to advance.
entries.icon_hint: a ruined stone courtyard with a small fireball arcing through the air

entries.name: Act 3: The Ramp
entries.description: A sloped area built around the game's signature rolling boulder (a direct Rec Room homage) - push it by walking into it, or punch it for a bigger shove, and let it roll downhill through a crowd. It instantly squashes any Goblin or Imp (or their Elite versions, and even a Goblin Knight) caught at speed, crediting the kill and its gold to whoever pushed it last; it can never hurt a player. Five area-triggered waves here are Goblin- and Imp-only (no Elites yet) - two waves of 6 Goblins bookend the act, with Imp-heavy waves of 2, 3 and 4 in between.
entries.how_to_use: Clear its enemy waves - line enemies up in front of the boulder and push or punch it into them - then gather at the exit door to advance.
entries.icon_hint: a large grey stone boulder rolling down a wooden ramp

entries.name: Act 4: The Bridge
entries.description: A long crossing that opens with the act's biggest pure-Goblin rush yet (5, then 7 in a row) before easing into mixed Goblin/Imp waves - and then, in its last two waves, introduces the Goblin Knight: a heavily armored, halberd-wielding enemy that can only be damaged from behind. Its telegraphed swing hits everyone in a wide arc in front of it and drops you in one hit, but the same instant it connects the Knight lunges forward and then freezes solid for 2 full seconds with its back exposed - that freeze is the entire opening a team gets to punish it. 3 Goblin Knights appear across the act's final two waves alongside more Goblins and Imps.
entries.how_to_use: Clear its enemy waves - bait a Goblin Knight's swing from the front, then punish the freeze from behind - then gather at the exit door to advance.
entries.icon_hint: a rickety wooden rope bridge spanning a chasm, with an armored goblin knight silhouette on it

entries.name: Act 5: The Split Path
entries.description: The path forks here, and this is where the Elite tier of the goblin army shows up for the first time: Elite Imp (a 1-shot Imp becomes a 5-fireball spread-shot, still stunnable by an arrow) appears in the very first wave, and Elite Goblin (immune to arrow stuns - melee or kiting only from here on) follows a couple of waves later. Seven waves total mix regular and Elite Goblins/Imps in increasing numbers, ending in a wave of 3 Elite Goblins + 2 Elite Imps together. Since Elite Goblins shrug off arrows, archers lose their easiest crowd-control tool starting here and need to lean on positioning instead.
entries.how_to_use: Clear all 7 waves across both branches, then gather at the exit door to advance.
entries.icon_hint: a stone path forking in two directions in a dungeon corridor, with a red-eyed elite goblin at the split

entries.name: Act 6: The Library
entries.description: A tall library area, entirely Elite-and-up from its very first wave (2 Elite Imps) onward - the last regular Goblins and Imps to appear in the whole run show up mixed into this act's third wave, after which nothing but Elites (and worse) remain. Its signature introduction is the Elite Goblin Knight: instead of one directional swing, it does a four-part spinning attack that sweeps almost the whole area around it in sequence, so there's no safe side to stand on during the attack itself - but afterward it freezes in place for a full 3 seconds, same rule as always: back only, and that freeze is your entire window. Seven waves total, peaking at a final wave mixing Goblins, Elite Goblins, Elite Imps and an Elite Goblin Knight together.
entries.how_to_use: Clear all 7 waves, then gather at the exit door to advance. Wait out an Elite Goblin Knight's spin rather than trying to interrupt it, then punish the freeze.
entries.icon_hint: tall bookshelves in a dim dungeon library with a glowing fireball reflected on the spines

entries.name: Act 7: The Maze
entries.description: The longest act by wave count (11 separate triggers) but individually one of the lighter ones - small, spread-out groups of Goblins, Imps and Elites rather than big simultaneous mobs, laid out through a genuine maze layout so enemies can trigger from unexpected angles as you route-find. A Goblin Knight makes a return appearance partway through alongside an Elite Goblin. The final two waves cluster Elite Goblins and Elite Imps together in a more open room at the maze's exit.
entries.how_to_use: Work through the maze clearing each small trigger group as you go, then gather at the exit door to advance.
entries.icon_hint: an overhead-style hedge or stone maze with dead ends and a single lit path

entries.name: Act 8: The Lava Room
entries.description: A large lava-crossed arena and the toughest gauntlet before the boss - 7 waves mixing every enemy type seen so far (Goblins, Imps and their Elite versions, plus both Goblin Knight and Elite Goblin Knight) in some combination, building to a final wave that throws Goblins, a Goblin Knight, Elite Goblins and Elite Imps at the room all at once. Its lava floor has a built-in safety net not seen in earlier acts: falling in cancels the usual instant death, knocks you down, and teleports you back to the last solid ground you were standing on instead - so a bad step here costs a knockdown and a teammate's time, not a life. Fall in three times in a row while already downed and you're sent back to the act's start point instead of being rescued in place.
entries.how_to_use: Clear all 7 waves, watch your footing around the lava (a fall here knocks you down rather than killing you outright), then gather at the exit door to advance to the boss.
entries.icon_hint: a rocky arena crossed by narrow stone paths over glowing orange lava

entries.name: Act 9: The Boss Arena -- the Goblin King
entries.description: The final act: a straight fight against the Goblin King, leader of the goblin army. Up close he uses the same telegraphed-swing-then-freeze pattern as a Goblin Knight (front-arc hit, one-hit knockdown, back-only damage, frozen and exposed afterward); at range he switches to a fireball volley instead. He's tough enough that a sword alone struggles to bring him down in time - a bow or crossbow from the armory helps punish him at range, and dual-wielding shields to eat his swings while a teammate works his back is a strong way to keep him permanently staggered. Three reinforcement waves join the fight automatically as his health drops past 75%, 50% and then 25% - a mix of Goblins, Imps, Elite Goblins, Elite Imps and a Goblin Knight escalating each time, so the room needs to keep an eye on adds even mid-boss-fight. He is also the network's only source of Cannon Ash, and one of only two sources of Orange Plastic - see the hub-materials file. Defeating him ends the run and shows the team's results (see Scoring and payout above for the coin/XP rewards, which scale with your S/A/B/C Quest Rating); separately, every 5th Diamond Trophy run you actually complete (clearing at least one act counts - beating the boss itself is not required) drops one random bonus item into your Bag, unrelated to that run's rating - see the items file's Run Completion Milestone Reward entry.
entries.how_to_use: Bring him down using back-hits during the freeze window after each telegraphed attack, using ranged weapons and shields to stay safe while a teammate gets behind him; watch for the automatic reinforcement waves at 75%/50%/25% health.
entries.icon_hint: a large armored goblin king wielding a crude sword and shield, flames flickering behind him

open_questions: The FistWatch home screen's "Rooms" tile can open a separate cross-server community rooms browser (built on the NetworkCore Rooms system), but that feature is switched off by default on this server, so today it opens the same Golden Trophy join screen as the "Diamond Trophy" tile. Worth re-checking if/when that browser goes live.

Room geometry, hidden shortcuts and exact spatial strategy tips (which pillar to hide behind, which corner is safest) weren't independently re-verified by walking the built world - only wave composition, enemy mechanics and gold/scoring numbers were confirmed against the live act configs and config.yml. Since this recreates the Rec Room original closely, some spatial tips from that original game likely still apply but may not translate exactly to this map's actual layout.

Corrected 2026-08-31: this file previously described the Act 9 win as granting "a reward (a treasure chest scaled by the run's Quest Rating)". Re-verified directly against DiamondThropyCore's source: no such item exists. Rating only scales the network-coins bonus; the sole per-run item payout is the Run Completion Milestone Reward (every 5th completed run, any rating, boss kill not required) documented in the items file.
